blocks.title: Oxidising and reducing agents
blocks.text: An oxidising agent (atom, ion or molecule) is a substance that oxidises another substance and is itself reduced to a lower oxidation state by gaining one or more electrons. A reducing agent is a substance that reduces another substance and is itself oxidised to a higher oxidation state by losing one or more electrons.

If an element gains one or more electrons and becomes an anion, X + e- giving X-, it acts as an oxidising agent, since it withdraws an electron from the other atom and its own oxidation number falls (0 to -1): for example Cl + e- giving Cl-. If an element loses an electron and becomes a cation, M giving M+ + e-, it acts as a reducing agent, since it provides electrons and its oxidation number rises (0 to +1): for example Na giving Na+ + e-.
In Fe2O3 + 3CO giving 2Fe + 3CO2, identify the species oxidised and reduced and the oxidising and reducing agents.
